items.title: Hedera Custodians Library
items.description: The hedera-custodians-library library is a Typescript utility designed to simplify custodial wallet management. It provides developers with tools to abstract complex aspects of custodial wallets, allowing them to focus on their application's core logic.

items.title: HTS Demo
items.description: This demo is a user interface written in Javascript (Vue.JS) to illustrate the use of the Hedera Token Service.

items.title: Hedera Smart Contract Starter
items.description: This project provides a hands-on demonstration of using upgradeable smart contracts with OpenZeppelin's upgrades plugins in Hardhat. Specifically, it is a smart contract starter project that illustrates the use of both Proxies and Beacon Proxies.

items.title: HCS Chat application
items.description: An example web app which demonstrates how you can use decentralized pub-sub messaging on the Hedera Consensus Service.

items.title: Proof of Action microservice
items.description: The Hedera Proof of Action (HPoA) microservice aims to make it easy for organizations to build a capability to record and subsequently prove the existence of business events using the Hedera Consensus Service.

items.title: Code snippets
items.description: Short, Self Contained, Correct Examples of code on Hedera.

items.title: Create React App Hedera Dapp Template
items.description: Hedera DApp Starter Template using Create React App, Material UI and Typescript with Hedera native wallet support and MetaMask wallet support.

items.title: Hardhat example project
items.description: This Hedera Hardhat Example Project offers boilerplate code for testing and deploying smart contracts via Hardhat. It includes configuration for both community-hosted and local (Hedera Local Node) instances of the Hedera JSON RPC Relay.

items.title: Hedera Subgraph Example
items.description: The Hedera Subgraph Example Project demonstrates how to create and deploy a subgraph to a local graph node using The Graph Protocol. Based on the Hedera Hardhat Example Project Repository.

items.title: Hedera DApp Integrated with WalletConnec
items.description: t - Explore DApp development using the Mirror Node API and Hedera Token Service (HTS). Discover how to integrate HTS functionality into your DApp for seamless token management and transactions. This guide uses React, Material UI, Ethers, and TypeScript with the Create React App (CRA) Hedera DApp template integrated with walletconnect, streamlining your development process.

items.title: Hedera DApp CRA Template
items.description: Hedera DApp Starter Template using Create React App, Material UI and JavaScript with HashPack, Blade, and MetaMask wallet support.

items.title: Risk Calculator for Hedera Tokens
items.description: Risk Calculator application serves as a tool to evaluate the risk associated with tokens on the Hedera network, specifically to assess the likelihood of a rug pull based on a token's properties. It calculates a risk score and levels by examining various risk factors like Admin Key, Supply Key, KYC Key, etc.

items.title: Airdrop Verifier
items.description: The Airdrop Verifier is a utility that simplifies the process of organizing airdrops for Hedera tokens. Users can input a Token ID and a list of account IDs to which they wish to airdrop tokens. The application generates a list of addresses either associated with the token or having available auto-association slots, ensuring efficient and targeted airdrops.

items.title: Rarity Inspector
items.description: This project allows users to upload a .zip file through a dropzone to check how NFTs are presented (displayed in a gallery as cards that can be clicked to read detailed information about them) and their "rarity". The project presents charts showing these data and several other features. Additionally, sorting and filtering options are available to simplify data browsing.

items.title: Token Holders List Builder
items.description: The Token Holders List Builder is a tool designed to efficiently generate lists of token holders who meet specific criteria, like holding a minimum number of NFTs from a particular collection. This can be especially useful for identifying key stakeholders or organizing targeted marketing campaigns within the NFT community. By automating what would otherwise be a complex data retrieval process, this tool simplifies analytics and community management for NFT projects.

items.title: Supra Demo on Hedera | Push
items.description: This example shows how to use Supra Oracles real-world data feeds (Push model).

items.title: Supra Demo on Hedera | Pull
items.description: This example shows how to use Supra Oracles real-world data feeds (Pull model). It fetches and verifies price data from Supra's gRPC server and use it within a smart contract on the Hedera network.

items.title: Example Pyth Oracle Contract Pull
items.description: This demo is a simple example of how to use Pyth prices in Hedera and is based on the tutorial here. Follow the instructions in the tutorial to build and deploy and use this demo.

items.title: How to Test a Solidity Event with Foundry
items.description: Foundry supports the use of cheatcodes. Cheatcodes allow you to go beyond testing the outputs of your smart contracts. They allow developers to manipulate the state of the blockchain, test for reverts, and events. In this tutorial, we will focus on the cheatcode vm.expectEmit to test a solidity event.

items.title: How to Deploy and Verify a Hedera Smart Contract with Foundry
items.description: Discover how to deploy and automatically verify your Hedera smart contract. Learn how to verify a pre-existing contract and check a contract's verification status.

items.title: How to Setup Foundry and Write a Basic Unit Test
items.description: Using an existing Hedera node project with the JavaScript SDK, learn how to set up Foundry to be able to leverage Forge, their command-line tool, to run your smart contract tests written in Solidity.

items.title: Vanilla JS Dapp Template
items.description: A decentralized application template in pure JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. It uses Vite as its build tool.
